P.text: AtomWallet supports a 77-byte signature format r || s || v || validUntil || validAfter; _validateSignature strips the final 12 bytes and verifies the owner signature only against userOpHash and the stripped 65-byte rawSignature; getUserOpHash excludes the signature field.
P.evidence_quote: `AtomWallet` supports a 77-byte signature format: `r || s || v || validUntil || validAfter`.

I.text: The validUntil/validAfter time-window suffix must be authenticated by the owner signature so it cannot be modified without invalidating the signature.
I.evidence_quote: The root cause is that the wallet does not authenticate the last 12 bytes.

V.text: The last 12 bytes are treated as unauthenticated metadata, so any relayer/bundler with a valid 77-byte signed operation can arbitrarily rewrite the time window (e.g., make it valid immediately, remove expiry with (0,0), extend or shorten it), enabling execution outside the signer's intended window.
V.evidence_quote: As a result, any relayer/bundler that has a valid 77-byte signed operation can arbitrarily rewrite the time-window suffix without invalidating the owner’s signature.
